children: Artificial intelligence could disrupt the digital economy in much the same way the internet once upended the physical economy, according to Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, Americas CIO at UBS.
In an interview with CNBC, she warned that the disruption risk from AI may be underappreciated by investors.
Hoffmann-Burchardi explained that UBS prefers "atoms over bits," favoring the physical economy over traditional digital assets.
"AI could disrupt the digital economy," she said, noting that AI coding could upend traditional software while AI agents could transform digital advertising and e-commerce.
On the earnings front, she identified a clear divide between companies sensitive to interest rates and those more resilient.

"The camp that is more resilient is not only driving the majority of the earnings growth this year—we believe that will continue," she said. "That camp is very much tied to the infrastructure buildout, the picks and shovels of AI, so that's semiconductors
Hoffmann-Burchardi pushed back against concerns that AI's growth cycle may be slowing, emphasizing that both agentic AI and physical AI are approaching inflection points.

"Both of these markets could quickly ramp up to hundreds of billions in revenue over the next five to ten years," she said, adding that accelerating private capital flows into the sector provide additional tailwinds for public company earnings.

For portfolio positioning, she recommended healthcare, biotech, and pharma as key diversifiers. These sectors offer defensive balance during periods when the AI CapEx trade comes under pressure while also standing to benefit from AI adoption over time.
"It's playing offense and defense at the same time," she said.

title: Healthcare, biotech, pharma are key diversifiers as AI disrupts digital economy – UBS
